accepted.sentence: In a living room alcove, the unit can fit between walls and make an otherwise unused recess practical.
A low arrangement in a child’s room lets young readers reach their own stories without climbing.
In a classroom, shared supplies can be placed within reach so pupils can collect them during activities.
An office may use separate sections for binders, keeping reference materials accessible near a desk.
Beneath a staircase, staggered heights can make use of space that would otherwise be difficult to furnish.
In a shop, displayed merchandise can face customers, helping them browse items without opening enclosed storage.
Set perpendicular to a wall, an open unit can divide a room while allowing light and sightlines through.
In a shared dormitory, personal objects can occupy separate levels, giving roommates distinct areas for belongings.
